title: Recursion · Writing, Debugging and Iteration
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: True or false? A base case must make another recursive call.
questions.feedback: False. A base case stops further calls and returns a result.

questions.prompt: Which symbol means logical AND in C#?
questions.feedback: && requires both conditions to be true.

questions.prompt: A loop repeatedly halves n starting at 40 using integer division. List the next three values.
PowerTwo(n) returns 1 when n = 0; otherwise it returns 2 * PowerTwo(n - 1). What does PowerTwo(3) return?

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: termination — Reaching a condition where the algorithm stops.
recursive step — Calling the function on a smaller or simpler input.
iteration — Repeating instructions using a loop.
stack overflow — Failure when active calls exhaust available stack space.
precondition — An input rule assumed by an algorithm.

blocks.title: C# worked example
Trace the calls
blocks.text: CountDigits(582) → CountDigits(58) → CountDigits(5). Returns are 1, 2, 3. For non-negative input the call moves towards the base case.

blocks.title: Compare with iteration
blocks.text: An iterative solution uses a while loop and reuses local variables. Recursive calls add active stack frames. Recursion can express tree traversal more clearly.

blocks.title: Independent practice

questions.prompt: What is PowerTwo(3) with base case 0 returning 1?
What may happen if recursive calls never reach a base case?
Which is normally more stack-memory efficient for simple repetition?
A recursive call should move towards a reachable base case.
questions.feedback: Progress towards a stopping condition allows the calls to finish.

questions.prompt: A simple iterative loop normally creates a new call stack frame for every iteration.
questions.feedback: A loop repeats in the same call; recursion creates additional active calls.

questions.prompt: Recursion can make tree traversal easier to express.
questions.feedback: Each subtree can be processed using the same recursive algorithm.
